name: Ping An Biomedical Co., Ltd.

profile.description: Ping An Biomedical Co., Ltd., formerly Majestic Ideal Holdings Ltd. (name changed September 2025, ticker changed from MJID to PASW), provides supply chain management services in the apparel industry in China, Hong Kong, Cambodia, and Europe. Services include market trend analysis, product design, raw material sourcing, production and quality control, and logistics management. In October 2025, the company underwent major leadership changes appointing Pijun Liu as Chairman and CEO. In January 2026, PASW secured strategic investments from Chinese tech and VC executives including 58 Group's Yao Jinbo to 'accelerate biopharma growth,' and signed a strategic cooperation agreement targeting RMB 500M in sales [1][2]. However, the company has only 7 employees and $0.13 stock price with a $16.94M market cap.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): The company's stated business of apparel supply chain management — sourcing, production, quality control, and logistics — faces moderate AI exposure [1]. AI-powered supply chain optimization, automated quality inspection via computer vision, and demand forecasting tools could partially displace the coordination services PASW provides. However, the physical aspects of textile manufacturing and garment production in facilities across China and Cambodia provide structural protection against full AI substitution. The company's announced pivot toward 'biopharma growth' is too undefined to assess AI resilience in any potential new business line [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI products, services, or revenue identified. The company shows no evidence of adopting or deploying AI in any capacity.

infinite_game.summary: Ping An Biomedical exhibits no meaningful characteristics of an infinite game player. The company has no articulated Just Cause, no evidence of courageous leadership decisions validated by execution, no organizational culture data, and no competitive mindset beyond survival. With 7 employees, collapsing revenue, a cosmetic rebrand, and complete leadership turnover in October 2025, this is a company in terminal decline or transitioning toward a shell structure [1][2]. The January 2026 strategic investment could represent a new chapter, but no operational evidence supports this.

The September 2025 name change from Majestic Ideal Holdings to Ping An Biomedical — without any visible biomedical operations, products, or capabilities — and the complete leadership overhaul in October 2025 suggest a company searching for a new identity rather than pursuing a cause [1][2].

The complete leadership turnover in October 2025 — new Chairman/CEO (Pijun Liu), new CFO (Hongli Yang), and new independent director (Xianzhi Liu) — and the 61% revenue collapse suggest significant organizational instability [2].

investment_thesis: There is no credible bull case for PASW. The company has 7 employees, a $16.94M market cap, and approximately $4.8M in TTM revenue after a 61% revenue collapse in FY2025 [3]. The September 2025 name change to Ping An Biomedical and January 2026 strategic investment from Chinese tech VCs (including 58 Group's Yao Jinbo) to 'accelerate biopharma growth' are the only constructive developments, but these have not been accompanied by any visible biomedical operations, products, or capabilities [2]. The Yuan Sheng Mei Yan cooperation agreement targeting RMB 500M in sales is aspirational but unsubstantiated. The stock at $0.13 reflects speculative optionality on the biopharma pivot materializing.
thesis_continued: PASW fails every IOWN quality screen. The stock triggers the liquidity floor with approximately $23,436 daily dollar volume versus the $1M minimum, rendering it untradeable for any meaningful position size [3]. The company is unprofitable (FY2025 loss of -$12.83M), has no dividend, no visible product pipeline, and no competitive moat. The name change to 'Biomedical' without any biomedical substance, combined with the complete October 2025 leadership overhaul and January 2026 VC investment, raises questions about whether this is an operating company or a shell vehicle for a future transaction. The stock has declined 92% from its 52-week high of $1.73 to $0.13. Any capital deployed here faces near-total loss risk with no identifiable path to value creation validated by operational evidence [3].
key_catalysts: If the biopharma pivot backed by Chinese tech VCs (58 Group's Yao Jinbo, Amiba Capital's Wang Donghui, Magcloud Group's Li Daxue) leads to genuine biomedical operations or partnerships, it could represent a transformative business model shift — but no operational evidence supports this currently [2]
Yuan Sheng Mei Yan strategic cooperation agreement targeting RMB 500M in sales could provide material revenue if executed, though no timeline or execution details have been disclosed [2]
Potential reverse merger or strategic transaction that could bring a viable business into the PASW listed shell, leveraging the Nasdaq listing and new investor backing [2]
key_risks: Liquidity floor failure — $23,436 daily dollar volume makes it impossible to build or exit any meaningful position without massive market impact [3]

Going concern risk — 7 employees, $16.94M market cap, negative earnings, 61% revenue decline, and 92% stock price decline from 52-week high suggest elevated probability of delisting, dilutive financing, or operational failure [3]

Corporate governance concerns — name change to 'Biomedical' without visible biomedical operations, complete leadership turnover in October 2025, and reliance on aspirational VC-backed strategy raise questions about management's intent and shareholder protection [1][2]
